title: Theme
description: A theme — a substantive grouping of codes, one level of abstraction below a category. Produced by `13-axial-coding`, stored in the Markdown card `3-analysis/themes/<slug>.md` (this JSON is the frontmatter + structured body).

theme_id.description: Unique theme ID within the project: T01, T02, ...

name.description: Theme name — a short phrase capturing the essence. NOT a textbook label ('motivations', 'pain points'), but specific to this product and these respondents.

slug.description: Name for the file system and wikilinks.

status.description: emerging — appeared after 1–3 interviews, may still change. stable — settled after 5+. saturated — new interviews add no material. merged — merged into another theme (see merged_into). deprecated — dropped during a rebuild.

merged_into.description: If status=merged — the ID of the theme it was merged into.

summary.description: 2–4 sentences on what the theme means and in which situations it arises.

category_id.description: ID of the category the theme belongs to (from `13-axial-coding`). null — not yet assigned.

axis_id.description: Axis ID, if the theme lies on one of the axes.

axis_pole.description: Name of the axis pole the theme is closer to. For example, 'explicit-control' on the 'control-over-the-process' axis.

supporting_codes.description: Flat codes (from `coded-segment.content_codes`) grouped under this theme.

supporting_respondents.description: Respondents for whom the theme appeared. Unique IDs.

supporting_segments.description: References to evidence segments. The quotes themselves live in `coded-segment.verbatim` — not duplicated here.

open_questions.description: What is still unclear about the theme; what to probe further in upcoming interviews.
